articles.title: Is Matt Olson being overlooked in the National League MVP race?
articles.summary: Matt Olson is putting together another monster season for the Braves, and his combination of power, production and consistency has pushed him into the Nation...
articles.body:
Is Matt Olson being overlooked in the National League MVP race? originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

Matt Olson isn't the favorite to win the National League MVP award.

But dismissing the Atlanta Braves first baseman from the conversation would be increasingly difficult.

Olson has put together one of the strongest seasons of his career, entering the final stretch with 36 home runs, 77 RBIs, 31 doubles and an .865 OPS. He has accumulated 4.1 Baseball-Reference WAR while once again providing Atlanta with durability in the middle of its lineup.

He has an argument. But right now, Pete Crow-Armstrong appears to have the stronger one.

MLB.com latest MVP poll placed Crow-Armstrong atop a crowded NL race, while Shohei Ohtani remains firmly in contention despite a knee issue preventing him from pitching since July 3.

Olson's case begins with power and consistency.

On Aug. 16, Olson launched his 36th homer of the season, a three-run shot that gave Atlanta the lead against Arizona . At the time, it also gave him an MLB-leading 66 extra-base hits.

Olson finished fourth in NL MVP voting in 2023 after producing 54 home runs and 139 RBIs. Braves manager Walt Weiss believes Olson might actually be a more complete hitter now, even if he doesn't match those massive power totals.

But winning MVP requires separating from elite competition.

Crow-Armstrong has combined power, speed and premium center-field defense into perhaps the NL's best all-around season. Ohtani remains one of baseball's most dangerous offensive players, and candidates such as Kyle Schwarber are also part of the discussion.

That's where Olson faces his biggest challenge.

A first baseman must produce overwhelming offensive numbers to overcome the positional value provided by an elite defensive center fielder such as Crow-Armstrong. Olson's 4.1 bWAR is excellent, but it doesn't currently separate him from the field.

If Olson finishes with a September surge, reaches or surpasses 45 homers and helps drive Atlanta through the stretch run, voters could look at his candidacy differently.

Right now, Olson shouldn't be called the NL MVP favorite.

But he absolutely belongs in the conversation.

And with more than a month remaining, the Braves slugger still has time to turn an MVP-caliber season into an MVP-winning one.

articles.title: Dominik Livaković on whether he’ll play for Barcelona this season: ‘We’ll see’
articles.summary: The goalkeeper is ready to put pen on paper
articles.body:
Dominik Livaković is set to sign for FC Barcelona , although it's still not clear whether he'll play for the Catalans this season or join Dinamo Zagreb on loan.

Barcelona already have Wojciech Szczęsny and Joan Garcia as goalkeepers, and there are rumors that they wanted to loan Livaković for a season while Szczęsny remains as backup to Garcia. However, competing whispers say that he could stay with Barça as Garcia's backup without going on loan first.

"I'm very happy to be here," the keeper said , having landed in Barcelona. When asked whether he would stay or go out on loan, he simply said, "we'll see."

The main deciding factor is reportedly whether Barça will have enough space within the FIFA Fair Play salary limit. If there's room, he'll stay, if not, he'll go out on loan and re-join in a year.

The keeper comes from Fenerbahçe, it's understood Barcelona will pay four million euro to sign him from the Turkish giants.

Livaković played on loan for Girona FC for the first half of last season before going on loan to Dinamo, his boyhood club, for the second half of the season.

He is a star for Croatia , having been their #1 keeper for two FIFA World Cups in which they finished 2nd and 3rd. In particular, he was a hero for Croatia in the 2022 World Cup, saving three penalties in a shootout victory against Japan and then producing eleven saves during the match, plus one in the shootout, in a win over Brazil .

articles.title: Yankees stars Aaron Judge, Max Fried taking steps in the right direction
articles.summary: NEW YORK — The New York Yankees shared encouraging updates on two of their stars before Tuesday’s series-opener against the Houston Astros, as Aaron Judge an...
articles.body:
NEW YORK — The New York Yankees shared encouraging updates on two of their stars before Tuesday's series-opener against the Houston Astros , as Aaron Judge and Max Fried have both taken steps in the right direction this week.

Judge, out since May 31 with a stress fracture in his first right rib, took batting practice in the cage and ran on Tuesday at Yankee Stadium, Aaron Boone said before the Bombers' 9-7 loss to Houston. Boone specified that Judge expected to see some overhand pitching on Tuesday. The back-to-back MVP previously hit off the tee and against soft toss.

The manager added that Judge also threw from over 100 feet and shagged fly balls while Fried and Brendan Beck threw live batting practice during Monday's off day.

It's unclear when Judge will take his next steps, but he's still a few away from getting into game action. Facing velocity and live pitching are among the items on his to-do list.

"He's got a calendar of what they're doing, but you make adjustments to that as you go," Boone said. "So definitely mapping things out, but as you check some boxes and move on, sometimes that progress speeds up a little bit. Sometimes you take a step back."

As Judge continues to progress, it will be interesting to see what his swing looks like. The location of his injury has led some to wonder if he'll be hindered — Judge did slump for a few weeks while playing through pain prior to going on the IL — but Boone didn't share those concerns on Tuesday.

"I haven't really asked that question," the skipper said when asked if he expects Judge to regain his bat speed and power. "My expectation is that he's going to be Aaron Judge."

The Yankees are counting on that, as they entered Tuesday with the worst wRC+ (87) and the second-fewest runs scored (274) since Judge last played. That was before their seven-run showing, which featured a three-run bomb from Cody Bellinger and a two-run shot from Luis García Jr., as well as poor performances from relievers Fernando Cruz and Brent Headrick .

Boone also expects to primarily use Judge in right field, even though he acknowledged that that "inherently" comes with more risk. While Judge could get some DH days here and there, the Yankees still need that slot for their surplus of DH/first base types: Ben Rice , Paul Goldschmidt and Luis García Jr.

That's the case even with full-time DH Giancarlo Stanton suffering yet another calf strain.

"I don't expect [Judge] to be diving or things like that, but [fielding] brings a greater risk than just swinging," Boone said. "Playing brings risk. But we're not going to put him out there where he's in jeopardy. If he's not ready to go, he's not ready to go."

As the Yankees eagerly await the return of their captain, their co-ace appears much closer to activation.

Fried, who returned to the IL on Aug. 17 with his second left elbow bone bruise of the season, threw 60 pitches over four simulated innings on Monday. Boone said that the lefty is "potentially" in play to start on Saturday, when the Yankees will host the Red Sox for a doubleheader.

"We'll see where we are as these next couple days unfold," Boone said.

Meanwhile, Yankees pitching coach Matt Blake said that Fried will likely be in the 60-pitch range should he return this weekend.

Getting Fried back so soon would certainly be a positive development for the Yankees, as he missed two months with his first bone bruise. The Yankees also just lost fellow southpaw starter Ryan Weathers to a flexor strain, so their rotation depth is a bit thin at the moment.
authors: Gary Phillips, New York Daily News

images.caption: Yankees stars Aaron Judge, Max Fried taking steps in the right direction (Jim McIsaac/Getty Images North America/TNS)

articles.title: How Australia trip makes roster cuts more difficult for 49ers
articles.summary: Kyle Shanahan just wants to make sure the San Francisco 49ers are fully healthy for their long trip down under.
articles.body:
With the San Francisco 49ers ' Week 1 trip to Melbourne, Australia, now about a week away, head coach Kyle Shanahan kept his focus on the logistics of getting there rather than the excitement of the matchup itself.

Asked how excited he is for the trip, Shanahan responded with some levity before turning serious.

"Trying to get me in trouble?" Shanahan said, laughing. "I'm just hoping our team's healthy enough and has the time to get there. Those are the challenges of it, just to get there to prepare for it. Guys still trying to recover to get there, the plane flight and things like that."

Shanahan has been candid about his reservations with the trip since it was first announced, previously saying he didn't see much upside for his team in playing an international game so early in the season. He's also noted the toll of the travel itself , with the 49ers set to log an NFL-record amount of mileage in 2026 partly because of the trip to Australia. Still, Shanahan struck a more optimistic tone Monday about what awaits the team once it arrives.

"But once you do get there and stuff, we're going to have fun playing in another country and it's going to be a cool atmosphere, things like that," Shanahan said. "That'll all be good. But right now, I'm just thinking of the challenges of getting our team ready for those three and a half hours."

San Francisco opens its season against the Rams on Sept. 10, with kickoff at 10:35 a.m. local time in Australia — 5:35 p.m. PT back home. The 49ers plan to depart nine days before kickoff to help players adjust to the 17-hour time difference, a stretch that will test the roster's health and preparation before the games even begin to count.

articles.title: USC countdown to kickoff: Recalling Trojans safety Kevin Ellison
articles.summary: Today, we look at a standout safety from the 2000s
articles.body:
Countdown to kickoff is back! USC will kick off its 2026 football season on August 29 when the Trojans host San Jose State at the Coliseum. In this series, we will be counting down the days until the season opener by highlighting a notable Trojan who wore each number.

With four days to go, today we look at former USC safety Kevin Ellison.

Carter highlights: After serving as a backup safety and playing on special teams his freshman season, Ellison became a starter as a sophomore in 2006, a role he would hold down for the next three years. He finished his career in Cardinal and Gold with 168 total tackles, five interceptions, three sacks, and three forced fumbles. Following both the 2007 and 2008 seasons, Ellison was named first-team All-Pac-10.

After USC: The San Diego Chargers selected Ellison in the sixth round of the 2009 NFL Draft. As a rookie, he appeared in 13 regular season games and one postseason game, recording 52 tackles and one sack. However, he was waived by San Diego during the 2010 offseason following an arrest for possession of a controlled substance. Ellison then signed with the Seattle Seahawks , reuniting him with his college head coach Pete Carroll, but did not make the team's regular season roster.

In October 2018, Ellison tragically passed away at the age of 31 after being hit by a car while walking along the highway. Although his death was ruled an accident, Ellison was posthumously diagnosed with CTE sustained from his football playing days.

We have the first team qualified for the Leagues Cup 2026 semifinals.

Rayados were the better side throughout the 90 minutes against the MLS team. Monterrey had the chance to take the lead but missed a penalty. But just minutes before the end of the first half, a great header from Guzmán gave them the lead.

articles.title: 66-67 – Rangers can’t climb over .500 after first inning from hell
articles.summary: A bad time for Jacob deGrom’s worst start as a Ranger
articles.body:
The Texas Rangers scored seven runs but the Chicago White Sox scored eleven runs.

In the top of the first inning, Wyatt Langford popped a ball straight up for what should have been an easy third out but due to poor communication from the White Sox infield, the ball dropped and the Rangers had their first base runner.

You could argue that Langford had time to end up on second base had he been sprinting but he settled for a single on the mistake. One batter later, Brandon Nimmo roped a ball down the line for a double. You would assume that, with two outs, Langford would be chugging around the bases to attempt to score.

However, Langford seemed to think the ball was either fielded by the Chicago first baseman or deflected closer to the infield or something because he just stopped at second base with third base coach Corey Ragsdale screaming at him to get moving.

By the time Langford realized the ball had reached the outfield, the best he could do was stop at third base, ruining a shot at two-out RBI and an early lead. The Rangers had another crack at that with Ezequiel Duran up with two men in scoring position but he elected to bunt with two outs for some inexplicable reason.

Now, obviously Duran was trying to catch the White Sox by surprise with a bunt but in addition to that being asinine as essentially Texas' most productive and dangerous hitter of the last few weeks or so was reduced to hoping for a surprise bunt hit, Duran's execution on the bunt itself was also poor giving the White Sox an easy out to wiggle out of danger.

Despite being gifted some golden opportunities, the Rangers wasted them and as bad as all of that sounds, I regret to inform you that the top of the first inning was far and away the better of the two halves for Texas.

In the bottom of the inning, Rangers starter Jacob deGrom allowed six runs on five hits and two walks. None of the six hits featured an exit velo of above 80 MPH. The furthest of the hits went was a 230 ft single that left Miguel Vargas ' bat at 71.5 MPH. All were weakly hit. Some were obnoxious bloopers.

It wasn't all tragic BABIP luck, though. The walks were killer and the frustrating sequence was compounded by Justin Foscue being unable to catch a throw and apply a tag that could have negated a leadoff double, and later Langford making one of the worst throws I've ever seen that turned into a throwing error that allowed Chicago to score their first run.

After that first inning, the Rangers outscored the White Sox 7-5 so I guess at least they battled and scored some runs. That will have to suffice for the silver lining for the evening. Unfortunately that first inning still counted and the Rangers are back below .500.

Player of the Game : Danny Jansen homered among his two hits and drove in a team-best three runs out of the No. 9 spot in the lineup.

Up Next : The Rangers will try to salvage a series win in tomorrow's finale with LHP MacKenzie Gore expected to make the mound for Texas opposite RHP Sean Burke for Chicago.

The Wednesday evening first pitch from Rate Field is scheduled for 6:40 pm CDT and will be aired on the Rangers Sports Network.

articles.title: ‘Never Praying on Anyone’s Downfall’ — Shedeur Sanders’ Brother Shilo Makes Feelings Clear on Deshaun Watson Reclaiming Browns’ QB1 Job
articles.summary: The decision by head coach Todd Monken to name Deshaun Watson the Week 1 starter against the Jacksonville Jaguars over Shedeur Sanders marks a high-stakes, v...
articles.body:
The decision by head coach Todd Monken to name Deshaun Watson the Week 1 starter against the Jacksonville Jaguars over Shedeur Sanders marks a high-stakes, volatile start to the Cleveland Browns ' season.

Amid fan frustration and a tense preseason, Shilo Sanders stepped forward with a grounded perspective on his brother Shedeur's backup role, in contrast to the surrounding media storm.

Shilo Speaks on Shedeur Sanders Vs. Deshaun Watson Denouement

The Browns' preseason centered on Watson and Sanders, with each quarterback starting one game.

Watson played well against Chicago , completing 11 of 15 passes for 126 yards, but struggled against Buffalo , going 5-of-12 for 36 yards and an interception. He was also booed by the home crowd and later termed the reaction "disrespectful" and "personal," sparking further discussion on his relationship with Browns fans.

Sanders showed promise in both appearances. He completed 6 of 11 passes for 79 yards and an interception against Chicago before going 9-of-11 for 74 yards, a touchdown, and an interception against Buffalo.

Despite Sanders' showings, head coach Todd Monken ultimately gave Watson the starting job, without allowing fan reaction to influence the decision.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

Shilo believes his brother's opportunity will come when the time is right. "It's a long season. Shedeur's time will come eventually, whether it's this year or next year, it doesn't matter. We never pray on nobody's downfall, and we wish the best for everybody.

"You're never going to succeed if you have bad intentions in your heart and your mind, and if you wish bad on somebody else. No matter what the situation is, that's not how you succeed," Shilo said .

Shilo's message was clear: Shedeur does not need Watson to fail to eventually earn his opportunity.

For now, Shedeur will have to remain patient and continue developing while Watson gets the chance to prove he can still lead the Browns.

START PREPARING: PFN's Free Fantasy Draft Simulator

Deshaun Watson Faces Pressure to Deliver

Watson enters Week 1 under significant pressure. Beyond the competition with Sanders, he needs to rebuild his relationship with the Browns fanbase, which has grown increasingly frustrated.

After the backlash over his comments following the Buffalo game, Watson acknowledged that his emotions got the better of him.

"I thought I was going to get a little different response. My emotions got the best of me. My comments weren't intended to go at any of the fans around in the city. Because there have been a lot of great fans that have been supporting me," Watson said .

The apology may serve as a band-aid, but Watson ultimately needs to produce on the field.

If he can play at a high level, the conversation around Sanders could quiet down. But another poor performance could quickly put Shedeur back at the center of the Browns' quarterback discussion.

articles.title: Kate Koval of Ukraine leaves LSU following the Tigers’ signing of a Russian player
articles.summary: Ukrainian center Kate Koval is leaving LSU less than two weeks after the Tigers brought in a player from Russia.
articles.body:
BATON ROUGE, La. (AP) — Ukrainian center Kate Koval is leaving LSU less than two weeks after the Tigers brought in a player from Russia.

LSU coach Kim Mulkey said Monday night that the 6-foot-5 Koval was leaving for "personal reasons," adding that the program will "respect her privacy on her decision."

"We had a long talk about it, and it was a hard decision for her," Mulkey continued. "I know it is hard because she loves LSU. Kate is a great person. She has to do what she feels is right for her, and we fully support her in that. We all wish her the best."

Koval, who was born in Kyiv, began her college career at Notre Dame. She transferred before last season to LSU, where she averaged 8.3 points and 6.3 rebounds per game.

LSU recently signed Anna Minaeva, a 6-5 post player who previously played professionally with MBA Moscow.

Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022 and the two countries have been at war since.

articles.title: Match day: Lexington SC at New Mexico United
articles.summary: Wednesday When: 7:25 p.m. Where: Isotopes Park TV/streaming/radio: New Mexico 50/ESPN+/FM-101.7 Records: New Mexico United (10-4-4), Lexington SC (9-7-4) The...
articles.body:
TV/streaming/radio: New Mexico 50/ESPN+/FM-101.7

Records: New Mexico United (10-4-4), Lexington SC (9-7-4)

Oh, look — a midweek matchup for New Mexico United.

The last time United played on a Wednesday? You guessed it, at Lexington on July 15.

And there will certainly be some things to keep an eye on in this meeting.

1. VIEW FROM THE TOP: That is the spot United now occupies in the 12-club Western Conference table despite its 0-0 draw at Loudoun United on Saturday.

New Mexico has 34 points, the same amount as second-place Orange County SC and third-place El Paso Locomotive FC. New Mexico, however, is currently in the No. 1 position due to tiebreakers.

The thing is, United could hold the spot without any help depending on what happens Wednesday.

A win or draw would obviously net the club three points or one, respectively, thus giving it more than either Orange County or El Paso.

But what the table looks like at the end of the night will depend on Locomotive, too. El Paso is also playing Wednesday. It's hosting Pittsburgh Riverhounds SC at 7 p.m. Those are the only two USL Championship matches happening.

Either way, it should make for an interesting — or maybe even exciting — midweek slate.

2. DIDN'T THESE TWO JUST PLAY? That's certainly what it feels like. But it'll be six weeks since New Mexico and Lexington played in Kentucky.

Forward Greg Hurst scored in the 42nd and 86th minutes. Midfielder Valentin Noël added a goal in the second minute of first-half stoppage time. Forward Joseph Melto hit the back of the net in the 68th.

Phillip Goodrum, meanwhile, scored for Lexington in the 70th to make the final look more respectable.

But New Mexico might have as many as three starters from that match out for Wednesday.

Melto received a red card at Loudoun, meaning he has to serve a one-match suspension. (Unless, of course, that decision was overturned by the league, which isn't likely to happen.)

The statuses of Noël and defender Maliek Howell are also in question. The two did not play in Loudoun after being designated with "lower-body injuries." Chances are any kind of update will be slim ahead of Wednesday's match, which is manager Dennis Sanchez's preference.

3. PERHAPS SOME MORE DEFENSE WILL HELP: Maybe it will be beneficial for Lexington.

The club announced the acquisition of defender Patrick Seagrist on Tuesday. Seagrist, who was loaned out by USL League One side Greenville Triumph SC, will be available for selection Wednesday.

The 28-year-old logged two assists in 16 appearances for Greenville. He's also played for New York Red Bulls in MLS as well as Indy Eleven, Memphis 901 FC, Colorado Springs Switchbacks FC and FC Tulsa in the USL Championship during his career.

Overall, Seagrist has made more than 150 appearances across the USL's different divisions and competitions. He's logged three goals and 10 assists.

4. WAIT, BACK-TO-BACK? Wednesday is the first of two consecutive home matches for United. Sounds strange, right?

United has not had back-to-back games at Isotopes Park since July 1 and 4, which came against Liga MX's Atlante FC in an international friendly and then Championship side Oakland Roots SC.

If you're looking for the last time New Mexico hosted clubs in just the Championship, you'd have to go back almost another month — Phoenix Rising FC on June 6 and Orange County on June 13. United beat Phoenix 4-0 in a USL Cup match and then drew 1-1 with Orange County in a regular-season matchup.

United forward Greg Hurst vs. Lexington keeper Oliver Semmle

Seems like a pretty obvious choice here. As noted above, Hurst recorded a brace the last time the two played. The keeper? That was Semmle. It's also worth noting Hurst has four goals in United's last five matches, started by that match in Lexington.

It wouldn't be surprising if Rennicks slides into Melto's spot in the starting lineup. It's what the forward did at Loudoun United when Cristian Nava, who was coming back from injury, was used as a substitute. Rennicks, however, has not scored in a regular-season match since the season opener at Oakland on March 14. He has not scored in any match since a win against AV Alta FC in a USL Cup matchup on April 25.

1: Surprise? United retained its top spot in the Championship's power rankings. It's the sixth straight week. Lexington is 10th in the 23-club Championship, up five places from a week ago.

100: United can earn its 100th regular-season victory by beating Lexington. New Mexico was unable to notch that milestone on Saturday at Loudoun United FC.

66: The number of saves United goalkeeper Kris Shakes has made in the regular season. That's good for third behind Birmingham Legion FC's Jaseem Koleilat (70) and Hartford Athletics' Antony Siaha (69).

18: The number of regular-season matches New Mexico has played. It's the fewest in the Championship.

David Glovach covers New Mexico United and other sports for the Journal. Reach him at dglovach@abqjournal.com or via X @DavidGlovach.

articles.title: Lobos position preview: DE Darren Agu giving Lobo defensive line a 'Freaks List' worthy presence
articles.summary: Last summer, Darren Agu had to make do with two trees for practice partners — one to practice his pass rush moves and the other to actually strike. “People w...
articles.body:
Last summer, Darren Agu had to make do with two trees for practice partners — one to practice his pass rush moves and the other to actually strike.

"People would walk by and look at me like, 'yo, what the heck? He's striking a tree,'" New Mexico's fifth-year defensive end laughed. "Leaves (were) falling down the tree, fruit, bugs. I'm like, 'you gotta get the strikes in somehow.'"

With a full offseason under his belt — one he was denied last summer — Agu believes he's playing at a "higher level" than he was in his first year with UNM.

In his first season with the Lobos, the former Vanderbilt transfer posted 15 total tackles, two sacks and 26 pressures, the third-best mark on the team. Agu, however, had to play catch-up for the entire year after visa issues kept him in his native London over the summer, holding him out of workouts and fall camp.

Before he made it back to Albuquerque in early September, Agu did his best with the equipment he had. He lifted and ran in accordance with the Lobos' offseason conditioning program. He watched the program's season opener against Michigan via FaceTime.

And in a public park, he found those two trees.

One passerby saw the towering 6-foot-6, 256-pound defensive end slamming his hands into the bark and stopped to ask if he was a rugby player.

"My forearms (and) my palms would be swollen, hitting the tree and stuff," Agu said. "But I was getting that work in, though."

This summer, Agu is reaping the benefits of a proper offseason. Off the field, he was named to the "Freaks List," an annual ranking of the freakiest athletes in college football by The Athletic's Bruce Feldman.

The list claims Agu benched 385 pounds and ran a 10-yard split in 1.61 seconds this offseason, a mix of power and speed that seems to be impress everybody but him.

"In the weight room, we do lifts and stuff and there would be times when I'd throw up a number," Agu said, "and (director of athletic performance Caleb Heim) and some of the strength coaches would be like, 'oh s***!' So I'd be like, 'is that crazy or something?'"

On the field? Agu is set to replace All-Mountain West defensive end Keyshawn James-Newby as UNM's starting Jack (boundary end) with a more pronounced presence as a pass rusher than last season.

Already a stout run defender, Agu has worked to become a more effective rusher through film study and walkthroughs.

"In the pass rush aspect, he's doing so much better (at feeling) and seeing what he's getting, and reacting to it," defensive line coach Hebron Fangupo said.

With fifth-year defensive end Brett Karhu currently ineligible, College of San Mateo transfer Albert Tuakalau is expected to start opposite of Agu. The 6-4, 245-pound junior flashed heavily this spring before cementing himself as one of UNM's top three defensive ends in camp.

Memphis transfer Jalen Charles, Copiah-Lincoln (Mississippi) Community College transfer Trenton Rocker and West Mesa graduate Elijah Brody are expected to provide further depth off the edge.

"He brings the Albuquerque grit and toughness," Fangupo said of Brody. "That's what gives him value. He's plenty athletic, he's got his speed, but man, he's a tough kid – if he had a choice, he'll run through your face."

On the interior, UNM will rely on defensive tackles Brian Booker, Jalen McIver and Xavier Slayton, who all logged 200-plus snaps last season. A preseason All-Mountain West selection, Booker said earlier this summer that he's looking to make more plays after leaving "a lot of meat on the table" last season.

Fangupo said he's proud of the 6-3, 325-pound fifth-year senior for his continued growth.

"He's gotten so much better in the mental aspect – being in control of what he can control and executing at a high level, penetrating low, fast and aggressive," he added. "But better yet, he's challenging his brothers to do the same … He's (running and finishing plays) more in practice and when he does that, we're so good, because he knows everything starts with the nose tackle."

Independence (Kansas) Community College transfer A.J. Robinson, sophomore Jake DeVos and Western New Mexico transfer – a La Cueva graduate and the older brother of Arizona State quarterback Cam Dyer – have helped provide depth on the interior.

"With Jalen and (Booker), we got some power out there … (Robinson and DeVos), they bring a different speed and agility to our play," Fangupo said. "And that's what we love about them – they are relentless, they play hard, play fast. But we gotta continue to bring them along."

Sean Reider covers college football and other sports for the Journal. You can reach him at sreider@abqjournal.com or via X at @lenaweereider.

articles.title: Duran’s Slam and Mickey’s Magic power the Red Sox to 7-3 extra-innings win in Miami
articles.summary: “I felt like a 100 pound weight was lifted off my shoulders.” — Jarren Duran after his tenth inning grand slam.
articles.body:
That's how Dan Secatore began the game recap here at Over The Monster after Saturday's heart-pounding win at Fenway . But you know what? That's becoming an increasingly appropriate way to start off every game recap around here.

Make no mistake, the Red Sox should have lost this game. They should have lost it when they gave the Marlins 14 at bats with runners in scoring position. They should have lost it when Payton Tolle ran out of gas at the end of his outing and allowed five of the last eight men he faced to reach base (including a Heriberto Hernandez home run). And they especially should have lost it in the bottom of the tenth when Aroldis Chapman wasn't available to close out a one run game and both Andruw Monasterio and Connor Wong made critical blunders that forced the bottom of the bullpen to get five outs in the inning.

Wong's egregious effort was specifically problematic because it should have ended the game. Wyatt Olds pitched his butt off and nearly got the equivalent of a four out save (I'm counting Monasterio's throwing error to lead off the inning as one of them), but because Wong couldn't move his butt on what should have been the final pitch of the evening, the ball went to the backstop and the Red Sox needed another inning to win the game.

Very, very rarely does a team recover from a play like this:

But this is the summer of 2026, and like a law of the universe that doesn't fully make sense, the Red Sox find inexplicable ways to win.

So of course, the Marlins go just 1-14 with the chances they had with men in scoring position. And of course, the leadoff double Payton Tolle gives up when he's teetering gets thrown out at third on the next play. And of course the Red Sox still manage to escape the tenth inning with Alec Gamboa on the mound. And of course they immediately follow that up with Jarren Duran grand slam in the 11th after he was hitless all night.

Here's the shot from Duran that proved to be the knockout blow:

But that wasn't even all of the magic, because before the game ever reached extras, the Sox were getting more incredible production from an unlikely source.

Normally when you're looking for Mickey Magic in Florida, you go to Orlando. Tonight, the Red Sox got it in Miami. Mickey Gasper went deep twice, and both to a deep part of the ballpark. Here's the first bomb:

You know what's crazy? Those Gasper home runs landed a little to each side of where Roman Anthony 's home run in the World Baseball Classic that proved to be the game winner against the Dominican Republic landed.

Speaking of Roman Anthony home runs, he was doing this in Worcester while all that was going on in Miami:

And while Andruw Monasterio was throwing the ball away in the tenth, Trevor Story was striking out on pitches like this:

I can't ever remember a night where two games at the MLB and Triple-A level were working in tandem to make a gaggle of upcoming roster crunch decisions more and more complex. This is wild stuff. What a night, what a team, what a summer!

Jarren Duran: Went straight from the dud pile (being 0-4 through ten innings) to the top of the stud mountain with his game winning grand slam.

Mickey Gasper: This guy had zero career home runs in a Red Sox uniform eight days ago. He now has five.

Erik Miller : Looked outstanding again as he struck out the side in the ninth. He still hasn't give up an earned run in the Red Sox uniform.

Wyatt Olds: Very rarely do we hand out studs to the guy who gets tagged with a blown save, but Olds deserved better as he essentially got four outs and was kneecapped by Monasterio and Wong. Over The Monster's own Jacob Roy will have more on Olds's inning tomorrow, so be on the lookout for that.

Andruw Monasterio: 1-5 at the plate, and the nearly crippling error in the bottom of the tenth. He did recover and field the final out however. (Now we await roster decisions to see if this was his final game of the 2026 season at the major league level.)

Connor Wong: He has to get in front of that ball in the bottom of the tenth. That's the type of play that makes me want Mickey Gasper as the backup catcher to Rutschman with Wong in Worcester.

Payton Tolle: As great as he looked early on, he was coming unglued at the end of the outing, and this is also kind of a big picture problem in the macro of the season. He's been better on longer rest all year, so how much does he have in the tank for late September and October? Navigating his usage will be incredibly tricky over the next few weeks (and hopefully next two months).

Duran's grand slam. So nice, it's worth seeing twice.

articles.title: ‘Holy fraud check’: Pros react to Bella Mir’s shocking upset loss on Contender Series
articles.summary: Bella Mir’s upset loss to Alex Apodaca had the MMA world buzzing
articles.body:
Bella Mir's upset loss sent shockwaves through the MMA world.

On Tuesday night, Mir ended up on the wrong end of one of the biggest upset losses in MMA history, dropping a unanimous decision to Alex Apodaca in the main event of Week 3 of Contender Series .

Daughter of former UFC heavyweight champion Frank Mir and an NCAA national champion in wrestling, Bella Mir was the biggest betting favorite in Contender Series history, coming in at -6000 in some places, but was unable to have much success with her wrestling and grappling and was outworked over 15 minutes by Apodaca.

At just 23 years old, this is likely only a setback for Mir, but given her outspoken stance before the fight, where Mir declared her intention to become "the best athlete of all time," Mir already had some detractors in the MMA community, who were quick to jump on the upset loss.

Check out MMA fighters' reactions to the shocking upset below.

articles.title: Jays Lose Another Frustrating Game
articles.summary: Royals 5 Blue Jays 3 Well, that was a frustrating game. As I said in the thread, we weren’t going to run the table. If they had to win every game left to get...
articles.body:
As I said in the thread, we weren't going to run the table. If they had to win every game left to get into the playoffs, it wasn't going to happen. They need to win most of their games, but not all of them.

That ninth inning……After two outs, Daz Cameron singled. Brett Bateman followed with a single and went to second on defensive indifference. Nathan Lukes singled them both home.

And then…..Lukes ignored the first base coach's stop sign and was thrown out trying to turn it into a double. This CAN NOT HAPPEN . His run didn't matter. If he score from second on a single, we would still be behind. He had to stop at first and hope that Vlad has another good at bat. You can not get thrown out at second when you aren't the tying run. I don't know what he was thinking.

The eighth inning was pretty much the tale of the season:

An out later, Jesús Sanchez was hit by pitch. Bases loaded for

Ernie Clement who, ummmm, fouled a ball off a part of the male anatomy that you really don't want to foul a ball off. He was down for a while. I was of the opinion they should take him out of the game. I know I wouldn't be able to hit after that. But, he stayed in and popped one to medium center. In the top of the ninth he dived for a ball and stayed on the ground for a bit, you know he was still hurting. Hitting a baseball is tough, hitting a baseball after being hit in the nuts, is impossible.

We had those two runs in the ninth and one in the first. Bateman and Lukes started the game with singles. An out later, Kazuma Okamoto walked to load the bases. Jesús Sánchez hit a sac fly. Clements followed with a strikeout.

Andrés Giménez hit a double to lead off the second, but we couldn't get him past third.

In the fourth, Clement and Giménez had one-out singles and Brandon Valenuela hit into a double play.

In the fifth, Bateman had a one-out single and went to second on an error, but ground out (Lukes) and flyout (Vlad) ended that.

In the seventh, Andrés Giménez was hit by pitch to start the inning, but Kirk hit into a double play.

And, well, we talked about the eighth and ninth.

Max Scherzer had a rough first inning, loading the bases on two walks and single, before getting his first out, but even with another walk, he only allowed one run. And he gave up another in the fifth. A one-out walk and two two-out singles scored the run, but he got out of it from there.

Five innings, four hits, two earned, five walks and four strikeouts. Which, other than the walks, was about the best we could hope from Max.

Braydon Fisher also had a rough time of it in the sixth, giving up two hits and as it turned out, two runs. But they weren't earned.

Mason Fluharty came in and Kyle Isbel put down a sac bunt, the runner from third wasn't coming out. But Vlad picked up the ball half way down the first base line, turned and threw side arm, well wide of Clement at first. One run scored. Quick play, but you have to make a better throw. Preferably not side arm (sidearm throws tend to slide to the arm side). A sac fly scored the other run.

Paul Swwald gave up a hit and two walks, but no runs in the seventh.

Brandon Little walked one, but had three strikeouts, in the eighth.

Tyler Rogers went single, steal, strikeout, ground out (runner to third) and single, scoring the run. I often say that the trouble with ground ball pitchers is that sometimes the ground balls find holes (of course the trouble with fly ball pitchers is some fly balls clear the fence, safer to strikeout everyone out).

We had 10 hits. Bateman had 3. Lukes and Giménez two. Okamoto, Sánchez (with a hit batter and a sac fly), Valenzuela/Kirk and Straw all had 0 fors.

1 for 11 with RISP just isn't going to cut it.

Other Award: Well, Lukes for going for second and ending the game, gets one. And Valenzuale (-0.15, plus a poor challenge, he also had a good challenge), Clement (-0.12, and he'll never have children again), Kirk (-0.10), and Straw (-0.10, but did make a great catch in left).

Tomorrow we have a bullpen day. As Jamie says, we've done very well in bullpen days. Of course, my objection to bullpen days isn't the game itself, it is the strain on the bullpen arms. Randy Dobnak (2-1, 1.58 ERA, in 9 games, 7 starts).

articles.title: Steelers sign hard-hitting former Pitt safety
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers have signed former Pitt strong safety Brandon Hill, the team announced on Tuesday.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have signed former Pitt strong safety Brandon Hill , the team announced on Tuesday.

Hill, 25, was a seventh-round pick of the Houston Texans in the 2023 NFL Draft and has bounced around the league from Houston to the Las Vegas Raiders and most recently, the Chicago Bears , who released him on Aug. 11.

A 5-foot-11, 195-pound native of Apopka, Florida, Hill redshirted in 2019, and became a regular in 2020 before starting in his final two seasons at Pitt in 2021 and 2022. He had three interceptions and nine passes defended over his Panthers career, including a pix six in 2020 against Florida State.
